tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate move legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before adding a move, check that the chosen disk is the topmost disk on its source peg and that moving it onto the destination peg does not place a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever generating a move, verify the move respects the Tower of Hanoi rules.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a disk that is not on top, or moving a larger disk onto a peg whose top disk is smaller.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary buffer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints; move it to a temporary peg to free its original peg or to hold it while larger disks are moved.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a peg needs to be empty for moving larger disks, or when you need a temporary holder for a disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 1 onto a peg that already has larger disks, then later moving it elsewhere.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat existing larger disks on target as base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the goal peg already contains some of the largest disks in the correct order, keep them untouched and build the remaining tower on top of them.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the goal configuration already has correctly placed larger disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 off the goal peg when it is already at the bottom of the final stack.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Iterative descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Assemble the final tower by handling disks from largest to smallest, placing each disk onto its goal peg before moving to the next smaller disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 2 onto the goal peg before moving disk 1 onto it, which would block later placement of larger disks.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the full sequence of moves, ensure the last syntactically correct list in the response is the move list, so the verifier can parse it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of the response, before any additional text.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving extra commentary after the move list, causing the parser to miss the list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Ensure source and destination pegs are clear of smaller disks before moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a larger disk, make sure its source peg has no smaller disks on top and the destination peg's top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When planning a move for a disk larger than the smallest.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 4 from a peg where disk 2 is on top, or moving disk 3 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 1.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Limit move list length to stay within token limits
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Generate a concise solution, preferably using the optimal or near‑optimal sequence of moves, to keep the move list short enough to fit within token limits.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the move sequence, aim for minimal or near‑minimal moves.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Producing an excessively long move list that gets truncated by the token limit.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Verify final configuration matches goal before outputting
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the move list, mentally simulate each move from the initial configuration to ensure the final state matches the goal configuration.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After completing the move sequence, before final output.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Missing the final move that places the smallest disk onto the goal peg, resulting in an incorrect final configuration.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive sub‑tower transfer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a stack of k disks from a source peg to a destination peg using the third peg, recursively move the top k‑1 disks to the auxiliary peg, move the largest disk, then move the k‑1 disks from the auxiliary to the destination.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When needing to relocate a sub‑tower of multiple disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move three disks directly without first moving the top two to the auxiliary peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear auxiliary peg of smallest disk before using it for larger moves
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a peg is needed as an empty auxiliary for moving larger disks, first move the smallest disk (or any smaller disks) off that peg, using another peg as temporary, to ensure the auxiliary is empty.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before using a peg as auxiliary in a recursive sub‑tower transfer, check whether it contains the smallest disk; if so, relocate the smallest disk elsewhere first.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 2 onto an auxiliary peg that still holds disk 1, causing an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generation before emitting any moves or forgets to include the list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always generate at least one move and ensure the move list is present as the final parseable list.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (size ordering violation)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a destination peg whose top disk is smaller than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check the destination peg's top disk (or emptiness) before moving a larger disk.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model picks a disk that is buried under other disks on its peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Verify that the chosen disk is the topmost disk on its source peg before adding the move.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The generated answer exceeds the token limit or the model stops early, cutting off the move list.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Keep the move sequence concise, aim for optimal or near‑optimal moves, and stop generation after the complete list.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk from a peg where it is not present
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model loses track of disk locations during mental simulation.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain an up‑to‑date mental representation of each peg after every move.
